what_it_is: A search box that lets store staff find any product in the catalog, instead of scrolling a list sorted by date.
headline: Staff now find the right product on the first try most of the time. Customers still see the old page, and one call about that is yours.

metrics.label: to find a product, down from 40
right product in the top three
old apps still on the old search

usage.goal: 150 of our 200 stores searching every week by Dec 1

gaps: Customer support tickets (no access from this session)

slides.question: Is this still the mission, and is the order on the roadmap right?
slides.context: Nobody has written the goal down since kickoff. I pieced this together from the kickoff notes and the roadmap file. If customers matter more than staff now, the plan flips.
slides.default: Keep this mission and this order.
slides.say: Before the news, a quick check that I'm aiming at the right thing.

slides.title: Search is live for every staff member
slides.lede: Anyone on staff can type a product name and get the best match first. Customers still see the old page.

stats.label: to find a product
stats.change: 34 s faster than the old page

stats.label: right product in the top three

slides.why: Store staff stop asking engineers to look products up for them.
slides.say: The short version: staff search works and they are using it. The customer page is the open question.

slides.question: Keep the search index in a single file, or move it to the main database now?
slides.context: I kept it in one file in week one to ship fast. It works, but a nightly rebuild now takes 40 minutes and blocks updates while it runs.

options.label: Keep the single file
options.consequence: No migration. The nightly rebuild keeps growing with the catalog.

options.label: Move to the main database
options.consequence: About two days of work. Rebuilds stop blocking updates.

slides.recommendation: Two days today. It gets more expensive with every feature we add on top.
slides.default: Keep the single file and raise it again next check-in.
slides.reversibility_note: Cheap until the filters land next week.

slides.title: The same search, before and after
slides.lede: The old page listed the newest products first, so the mug a staff member wanted sat at the bottom. Now it comes first.

before.alt: Old results: gift cards and towels above the mug
before.label: Before

after.alt: New results: the blue mug first, close matches below
after.label: After

visual.caption: Drag the handle. Same query on Oct 10 and today.

slides.why: The first result is the one they wanted, so nobody scrolls.

slides.data_from: search event log, Sep 22 to Oct 26
slides.title: 112 of 200 stores search every week, behind the pace for December
slides.lede: Use grew fast after launch, then flattened. At this rate about 130 stores search weekly by Dec 1, short of the 150 we aimed for.

points.text: Stores that try it stick: 9 in 10 come back the next week
Night shifts search three times as often as day shifts
Two stores' handheld scanners never report searches, so their use is invisible

visual.caption: The dashed line extends the last three weeks in a straight line.

slides.why: Stores that start keep going, so the gap is the stores that haven't tried it yet.
slides.say: Adoption is real but stalling. The fix is reaching the 88 stores that never opened it, not making search better for the ones that did.

evidence.label: Event log: distinct stores with a staff search, per week
Repeat use: stores active one week and also the next

slides.title: Three questions to store staff would settle the next month of work
slides.lede: Each answer changes what I build next. Tick the ones worth sending and I'll put them in the weekly store email.

asks.question: What made you go back to the old way?
asks.learn: Whether the 88 missing stores need training or a better search.
asks.how: Two-line email to the 40 store managers

asks.question: What do you search for most at night?
asks.learn: Whether night restocking needs its own shortcut.
asks.how: One-tap poll on the search page after 8pm

asks.question: Would you look this up yourself on your phone?
asks.learn: Whether the customer launch is worth doing before filters.
asks.how: Staff ask five customers each this week

evidence.label: Usage slide: stores that never came back

slides.title: When the mug is sold out, show what's on the shelf instead
slides.lede: Today a sold-out item still tops the list and staff scroll to find something in stock. This mock moves two in-stock lookalikes up and says when the original is back.

before.alt: Today: the sold-out mug first, lookalikes below
before.label: Today

after.alt: Mock: sold-out mug marked, two in-stock lookalikes on top
after.label: Mock

visual.caption: Drawn by hand, nothing is built. Same query as the before and after slide.

slides.why: Staff in two stores asked for exactly this, and it targets the stores that tried search once and stopped.
slides.cost: About three days, using stock levels we already load.

evidence.label: Store feedback form, Oct 21 and Oct 24

slides.question: Turn on the new search for customers this month?
slides.context: Staff results are good. Customers type differently, and we have not tested with them. A launch is public, so I won't do it without you.

options.label: Launch to 10% of customers
options.consequence: Real customer data in a week. Easy to switch off.

options.label: Launch to everyone
options.consequence: Fastest. A bad ranking day hits every customer.

options.label: Wait for filters
options.consequence: Launch in about three weeks with filters included.

slides.recommendation: A small launch tells us how customers search without betting the store on it.
slides.default: Wait. Nothing customer-facing changes without your call.
slides.reversibility_note: Customers see it the moment it is on.

next: Moving the warehouse scanner to the new search

mission.statement: Every store's staff can find any product in seconds, so customers get an answer at the shelf instead of a shrug.
mission.progress: Step one shipped. Step two is at 112 of 150 stores and stalling, so the customer launch is the next real call.
mission.source: Kickoff notes, Sep 12, and the roadmap file
